newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai grain/oilseed market quiet, buyers sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Thai grain/oilseed market quiet, buyers sidelined.

text.p: The Thai grain and oilseed c&f market was mostly inactive over the past week as most buyers were already covered, traders said on Tuesday.
"There was not that much activity in the market. Most buyers seemed to have enough supply for the next couple of months," said one Bangkok-based trader.
Buyers are also expected to delay any new buying this week and await lower prices following a drop in soymeal and soybean prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT), they said.
"They (buyers) now expect the (soymeal and soybean) prices to decline further after yesterday's fall on the CBOT," said another trader.
Low-protein South American soymeal was indicated around $325 per tonne c&f Bangkok, down from $333 this week, traders said. Local soymeal was quoted at 9.80-10.10 baht ($0.38-$0.39) a kg.
Local buyers were also awaiting a shipment of about 58,000 tonnes soymeal from South America scheduled to arrive on May 18, traders said.
Local corn prices edged up further this week to 4.80-5.10 baht a kg from 4.70-4.90 as buyers, mainly poultry exporters, continued to fill their requirements.
